name: Burundi
tagline: The southernmost source of the Nile
summary: A country of hills above Lake Tanganyika, with the drummers of Gishora on the UNESCO list, chimpanzees at Kibira, and a marker at Rutovu on the ridge where the Nile's longest tributary begins.
when: The long dry season, June to September.

entries.caption: Hills and Lake
entries.description: Every horizon is a ridge, and Tanganyika is at the bottom of all of them.
entries.subject: terraced green hills running down towards Lake Tanganyika

entries.caption: The Congo-Nile Divide
entries.description: A ridge running the length of the country, with the Nile on one side and the Congo on the other.
entries.subject: the forested ridge of the Congo-Nile divide under cloud

entries.caption: Chimpanzees at Kibira
entries.description: Montane forest continuous with Rwanda's Nyungwe, with chimpanzee and colobus in it.
entries.subject: a chimpanzee in the montane forest canopy at Kibira

entries.caption: Rusizi and Ruvubu
entries.description: Hippo and crocodile in the Rusizi delta, and buffalo and antelope along the Ruvubu.
entries.subject: hippos in the Rusizi river delta near Bujumbura

entries.caption: Mount Heha
entries.description: 2,684 metres, an hour from the capital, with the whole rift visible from the top.
entries.subject: the view from Mount Heha across ridges towards Lake Tanganyika

entries.caption: Karera
entries.description: Four falls in one forested gorge in the southeast, with a path between them.
entries.subject: the Karera falls dropping through forest in southern Burundi

entries.caption: Lake Tanganyika
entries.description: The second deepest lake on earth, and Burundi has a hundred and sixty kilometres of it.
entries.subject: the deep blue water of Lake Tanganyika from a hillside

entries.caption: Saga and Karera Beaches
entries.description: White sand on Tanganyika south of Bujumbura, with the Congo visible across the water.
entries.subject: white sand and palms on the shore of Lake Tanganyika

entries.caption: Kibira
entries.description: Forty thousand hectares of montane forest on the divide, and the country's water tower.
entries.subject: mossy montane forest and tree ferns at Kibira

entries.caption: Walking the Divide
entries.description: Kibira on foot, Mount Heha in a morning, and the lake shore road south.
entries.subject: a forest path along the ridge at Kibira

entries.caption: The Drums
entries.description: The royal drummers of Gishora are on the UNESCO list, and they are not a performance troupe.
entries.subject: Burundian royal drummers with drums on their heads

entries.caption: Hutu, Tutsi and Twa
entries.description: One language, Kirundi, spoken by everybody, and a history the country is still working through.
entries.subject: a village gathering under a tree in the Burundian hills

entries.caption: Beans, Ugali and Mukeke
entries.description: Beans and plantain, ugali, and mukeke — a Tanganyika fish grilled on the beach.
entries.subject: grilled mukeke fish with plantain on a plate

entries.caption: Gishora
entries.description: The drum sanctuary above Gitega, where the drums are kept and danced on their own ground.
entries.subject: drummers performing at the Gishora drum sanctuary

entries.caption: Basketry and Drums
entries.description: Coiled agaseke baskets with pointed lids, and the drums themselves.
entries.subject: coiled agaseke baskets with conical lids

entries.caption: Rutovu
entries.description: A stone pyramid on a ridge marking the southernmost source of the Nile.
entries.subject: the stone pyramid marking the Nile source at Rutovu

entries.caption: The Ritual Dance of the Royal Drum
entries.description: Inscribed in 2014 — the drums, the dance and the making of them, together.
entries.subject: a drum being carved and stretched at a Burundian workshop

entries.caption: Bujumbura and Gitega
entries.description: A lakeside city with a long promenade, and the political capital up in the hills.
entries.subject: the lakefront and hills at Bujumbura

entries.caption: Colonial and Hillside
entries.description: German and Belgian colonial in Bujumbura, and tiled hillside houses everywhere else.
entries.subject: a Belgian colonial building in central Bujumbura

entries.caption: The Beach on a Sunday
entries.description: Bujumbura goes to Saga beach, and stays until the light goes.
entries.subject: crowds at Saga beach on Lake Tanganyika on a Sunday

entries.caption: Lake and Hills
entries.description: Short distances, calm fresh water, and hippos to keep an eye on.
entries.subject: children playing on the sand at a Lake Tanganyika beach

entries.caption: Hiking the Hills
entries.description: Heha, Kibira and the ridge roads, none of them more than a day.
entries.subject: a walker on a ridge path above terraced hills

entries.caption: Modest
entries.description: A handful of hotels in Bujumbura, and lodges on the lake shore.
entries.subject: a lakeside hotel terrace at Bujumbura

entries.caption: Kibira's Water
entries.description: The forest feeds the hydro that runs most of the country, and protecting it is not sentiment.
entries.subject: a clear stream running out of Kibira forest

entries.caption: Drums in Motion
entries.description: Gishora mid-performance, when the drums are carried and struck at once.
entries.subject: a Burundian drummer leaping with a drum in performance

entries.caption: Rusizi Delta
entries.description: Hippos, birds and the Congo across the water, twenty minutes from the capital.
entries.subject: hippos and birds in the Rusizi delta at dusk

entries.caption: Why Burundi
entries.description: The Nile's furthest source, the royal drums, and a lake almost nobody visits.
entries.subject: a fishing boat on Lake Tanganyika below green hills
